subject: BrightPay: Post-demo recap & proposed reliability tests
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: BrightPay: Post-demo recap & proposed reliability tests

Claire — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and a proposed test plan to validate the reliability differences we discussed versus hyperscaler-managed endpoints. High level: BrightPay wants predictable latency, clear error budgets, and failover behavior that keeps payroll jobs moving during incidents.

Recap from demo:
- Redwood hosted endpoint showed consistent p95 latency in our demo model under realistic payroll batching (we used sample job sizes from your team).
- Key differentiators we highlighted: prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost and latency on repeated customer prompts; automatic model fallback when a variant is degraded; per-tenant throttling with graceful 429 + Retry-After.

Proposed reliability & competitive tests (we recommend a 3-day window):
1) Failover simulation (controlled instance preemption) — validate auto-fallback to variant model and effect on tail latency and success rate. Acceptance: no more than 2x p95 increase and <2% request error spike during transition.
2) Rate-limit ramp (sustained and burst) — ramp to 10x expected peak to exercise token-bucket behavior and observe 429 surface, retry behavior, and request shaping. Acceptance: <=1% of successful requests receive 5xx; 429s contain Retry-After and are within expected backoff.
3) Error-budget burn test — sustained injected 500s on a subset of nodes to quantify error-budget consumption and alerting cadence. Acceptance: alerts within configured windows and automated fallback if budget exceeded.

Attachments: detailed SLO summary and the failover runbook for Redwood's hosted stack.

Next steps: please confirm a 3-day testing window (we suggest Mar 3–5) and whether BrightPay can provide a small set of production-ish payloads (anonymized). Also let us know the hypothesis you'd most like to validate (latency profile, failover speed, or cost/throughput tradeoffs).

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call to align tests.

— Monica

Claire — great questions, answered inline below. I’ve attached a short SLO summary that you can pass to procurement; we marked negotiable items. Also included is a runbook and a small set of test scripts you can run if you prefer to originate traffic from BrightPay.

Failover behavior vs hyperscalers
- Hyperscaler-managed endpoints typically re-route to healthy nodes but they often use coarse-grained variants and can incur cold-start penalty when a model variant is activated. Redwood uses a combination of warm-KV cache caching and fast variant spin-up (sub-10s for warm model caches in most of our recent internal runs) and automatic fallback to quantized variants if the primary is unavailable. In practice this reduces transition tail-latency compared to unmanaged variant swaps.

Concrete SLOs (proposed, included in attached PDF):
- Availability (SLO): 99.95% per calendar month (target SLA negotiable)
- Monthly error budget (allowed downtime-equivalent): ~21.6 minutes (0.05% of month)
- P99 latency target under expected load: <= 700 ms for typical payroll prompt sizes (we’ll calibrate with your payloads)
- Alerting: automated on 15-minute rolling windows when error-budget consumption exceeds 20%

Rate limiting details
- Default tenant-level shaping: token-bucket with burst window. Default parameters we use for demos: burst up to 4k rps, sustained 600 rps per dedicated shard (configurable). When limits hit, clients receive 429 with Retry-After and we surface structured retry hints through the SDK.

Test harness
- Attached test scripts include both a Redwood-driven harness (we can run from our infra against a test tenant) and a client-side script you can run locally. We recommend Redwood run the first pass so we can coordinate internal node preemption without surprising your downstream monitors.

Next actions I’m proposing:
- You confirm a tentative 3-day window (Mar 3–5 or Mar 10–12) and whether EngOps can provide anonymized payloads.
- Aditya will coordinate the load plan and share a detailed ramp schedule.
- Procurement: Marissa can annotate SLOs and flag negotiable terms for your legal team.

Attaching: redwood-slo-summary.pdf (annotated with negotiable items), redwood-failover-runbook.md, test scripts. HubSpot has the deal attached for your reference: BRIGHT-2026-001.

— Monica

Folks — forwarding Claire’s note and our follow-up. BrightPay is asking for the SLOs and a coordinated three-day test window. Action items:

- Aditya: please build the detailed ramp plan for the rate-limit ramp and failover simulation. Include exact traffic profiles (payload sizes, concurrency, burst timing) and the times we’ll preempt nodes. I’ll coordinate with BrightPay EngOps so they can mute downstream alerts.
- Marissa: please review the attached SLO PDF and mark anything we should flag as negotiable from a commercial/legal POV. Claire called out procurement wants clear SLA vs SLO language.
- Ops coordination: I’ll schedule a 30-minute prep call with BrightPay (propose Mon 23rd 11am PT) to walk through the runbook.

Quick notes for the test plan (my suggestions):
- Failover run: simulate 2 separate preemptions during daytime traffic and measure p95/p99 delta and error spike length. Verify automatic fallback to quantized variant.
- Rate-limit ramp: 10–15 minute ramps to peak, hold for 30 minutes, then step down. Track 429 vs 5xx rates.
- Observability: ensure tracing headers are passed so we can correlate request ids across retries.

I’ll attach the test scripts and SLO PDF to the calendar invite. Let me know if you want to shift the prep call time.

— Monica
